free_tier.stated: 10 MB per attachment on Free, 250 MB on Standard. And explicitly 'there is no total limit for storage, just a per-file limit'.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.notes: extracted from the quota or limits prose

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: free direct download links, Atlassian CDN; no egress metering published

tooling: documented Trello REST API: POST /1/cards/{id}/attachments (multipart file or url), plus GET /1/cards/{id}/attachments; py-trello and trello-rclone-style wrappers exist
chaining: unlimited cards x 10 MB x unlimited boards x unlimited free Workspaces (10 members each). This is genuinely 'per-record unlimited': no bucket cap, only a per-file cap. 500 GB = 51,200 attachments
limits_note: 10 MB/file on Free; per-board attachment ceiling exists in the API response model (limits.attachments.perBoard warnAt 32400 / disableAt 36000). I.e. ~32k attachments/board before hard stop; 10 MB is small for bulk data.
reliability_note: attachments are real copies inside Trello ('Attachments from your computer create an actual copy within Trello'); Atlassian has deprecated/changed API auth (key+token still works) but attachments have been stable for a decade
confidence_note: Unverified: carried from historical research records without live verification. A first-party page read confirms documentation.
